story.headline: No. 5 Notre Dame seeks a reset against Navy after a controversial loss at BYU

Notre Dame has won eight consecutive games in the series, with Navy’s last win coming in 2016.

story.headline: No. 3 Georgia braces for test against No. 17 Florida as 'Outdoor Cocktail Party' moves to Atlanta
paragraphs: The World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party will have a different feel on Saturday when No. 3 Georgia plays No. 17 Florida in Atlanta for the first time.

The usual neutral site setting of Jacksonville, Florida., is not available due to renovations at EverBank Stadium. Instead, the 50-50 split of tickets at Mercedes-Benz Stadium may provide a setting similar to the Southeastern Conference championship game.

“This is my first experience around this game,” said Florida first-year coach Jon Sumrall. "I know it’s traditionally in Jacksonville. I think you have to know that Atlanta is not necessarily our backyard, right? But the 50-50 thing is a unique deal that I think is exciting for our guys because you’re in kind of a different environment than a normal SEC game, which is fun.”
Georgia is 8-2 in the rivalry under coach Kirby Smart, including wins in the last five games.

story.headline: No. 4 Indiana hoping to jump start its sluggish offense when it hosts surprising Minnesota
paragraphs: The Indiana Hoosiers offense has suddenly stalled.

And last week, at Michigan, Josh Hoover completed just eight passes for 81 yards before running for a 4-yard touchdown in overtime to the give Hoosiers a 13-6 victory.

So with a November run looming and the defending national champs hoping to make a third straight playoff appearance, the fourth-ranked Hoosiers want to find a solution Saturday when they face Minnesota and coach P.J. Fleck, who sees few flaws in his next foe.

“They’re two of the best (receivers) in the country on one team," Fleck said. "That’s a luxury that they have, that they use, and they’re very good in the run game, too, which I don’t think they get enough credit for — how well and how hard (the receivers) block on the perimeter, which allows all their dynamic backs to come shooting out on the second level and finish runs.”

story.headline: No. 6 Utah looks to remain unbeaten against upset-minded Cincinnati with both coming off big wins
paragraphs: Sixth-ranked Utah owns the nation's longest active winning streak and sits atop the Big 12 standings following last week's win over No. 18 Houston. Cincinnati, the Utes' next opponent, handed Texas Tech its first loss of the season in dominant fashion last week.
That's the cautionary tale Utes coach Morgan Scalley sent to his players ahead of Saturday's game.

“You get teams that have unbelievable wins, emotional wins, and then the next week you have the letdown effect,” Scalley said. “We’re just going to continue to preach that every game is a championship game because it’s hard to win. We have a great team in Cincinnati that we’re facing. They just beat a top-10 program in the country, Texas Tech and now they're hosting another one."

The Utes are 7-0 for the first time since 2010 and the ninth time in program history. They have won 13 straight games dating to 2025, the longest active streak in FBS and Utah's longest since it won 16 straight from Dec. 20, 2007, to Sept. 12, 2009. Utah has won nine straight Big 12 games.

story.headline: No. 2 Ohio State has everything but a starting QB in place for its visit to desperate USC
paragraphs: Ohio State is in Southern California this weekend with the No. 2 ranking, a sturdy defense and the nation's best receiver to face an opponent on the verge of disarray.
Seems like the only thing the Buckeyes (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) don't have is a starting quarterback.

Coach Ryan Day isn't saying whether Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair will be behind center against desperate USC (6-2, 3-2) in a sold-out Coliseum on Halloween night. The Buckeyes are in this jam because Julian Sayin injured his throwing arm two weeks ago in a gritty 19-15 victory over national champion Indiana.
After a fortuitous bye week to coach up Sayin's replacements, Day is optimistic the Buckeyes can overcome this central uncertainty in their first trip to the Trojans' historic stadium since 2008.
